summary: Johann Tobias Beck (1804–1878) worked in religious studies and philosophy. After studying at the University of Tübingen (ca. 1822–1826), he held academic posts at the University of Basel (ca. 1836–1843) and the University of Tübingen (ca. 1843–1878).

Johann Wilhelm Andreas Pfaff (1774–1835) was a scholar of Indology and other fields. He studied at the Tübinger Stift and University of Tübingen, holding posts at Tartu, Melanchthon-Gymnasium Nürnberg, the University of Würzburg, and Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg.

Johanna Engelberta van Lohuizen-de Leeuw (1919–1983) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied at Leiden and under Jan Gonda at Utrecht, later teaching at Groningen and Cambridge before directing the Institute of South Asian Archaeology at the University of Amsterdam.

Johanna Narten (1930–2019) was an Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian scholar. She studied under Ernst Zinn at Saarland University and completed her PhD under Karl Hoffmann at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg, where she later worked as an assistant (1973–1977).

Johannes Beltz specializes in Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral studies by 1999 at the University of Lausanne and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under the supervision of Marie-Louise Reiniche and Johannes Bronkhorst.

Johannes Bronkhorst (1946–2025) studied at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, University of Rajasthan, Pune University under Shivram Dattatray Joshi, and Leiden University. A scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, he served as a professor at the University of Lausanne from 1987.

Johannes Gijsbertus de Casparis (1916–2002) specialized in history, archaeology, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Leiden University (ca. 1934–1939) and later held posts at SOAS University of London (ca. 1965–1981) and Leiden University (1978–1986).

Johannes Hertel (1872–1955) was an Indology scholar who earned his doctorate from Leipzig University. He taught at Lessing-Gymnasium Döbeln before holding the chair of Indian philology at Leipzig University from 1919 to 1937.

Johannes Klatt (1852–1903) was an Indologist who studied under Albrecht Weber and earned his doctorate at the University of Halle. Beginning in 1872, he worked at the Prussian State Library, serving as custodian and later as librarian from 1889.

Johannes Nobel (1887–1960) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his doctorate under Heinrich Lüders at Berlin, worked at the Prussian State Library and Berlin, and held the Indology chair at Marburg from 1928 to 1955.

Johannes Rahder (1898–1988) worked in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Indology. After earning his doctorate at Utrecht University, he held posts at Utrecht, Leiden University, the University of Hawaiʻi, and served as professor at Yale University from 1947 to 1965.

Johannes Schmidt (1843–1901) specialized in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Bonn and Jena under August Schleicher and Albrecht Weber. He held posts at Bonn, the University of Graz, and became professor at Humboldt University of Berlin in 1876.

Johannes Schneider (born 1964) is a scholar of Indology and Tibetology. He completed his Magister at the University of Marburg, followed by posts at the Free University of Berlin, the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and the University of Munich.

Johannes Schubert (1896–1976) was a scholar of Tibetology and sinology who studied at Leipzig University. He worked at the Leipzig University Library, held teaching posts in Tibetan and Mongolian at Leipzig University, and worked for the Ahnenerbe (ca. 1939–1945).

John A. Ardussi is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied for his MA under Turrell V. Wylie, earned his PhD at the Australian National University (attested 1977), and served as a research team member at CNRS.

John Alexander Jorgensen works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology. Supervised by Kenneth Herbert Joseph Gardiner, he earned his MA at the Australian National University, where he later held posts, and was senior lecturer at Griffith University (attested 2012).

John Alexander Stewart (1882–1948) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at the University of Aberdeen, served in the Indian Civil Service (ca. 1905–1933), and later was Reader in Burmese at SOAS, University of London.

John Allan (1884–1955) was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist educated at Edinburgh and Leipzig. He served as Keeper of Coins and Medals at the British Museum and lectured in Sanskrit at University College London, SOAS, and the University of Edinburgh.

John Avery (1837–1887) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. Educated at Amherst College, Tübingen, and Berlin, he also studied under William Dwight Whitney. He later served as Professor of Greek at Grinnell College and Bowdoin College.
John B. Carman (born 1930) is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He served as director at Harvard University (attested 1999) and director of the Center for the Study of World Religions.
